newsitem.title: USA: Former Carter adviser Charles Kirbo dies at 79.
newsitem.headline: Former Carter adviser Charles Kirbo dies at 79.

text.p: Charles Kirbo, a longtime adviser to former President Jimmy Carter, died Monday at age 79 from complications from recent surgery.

Kirbo "was my closest friend," Carter said in a statement. "Without his wisdom, sound judgment, and guidance, I never would have been a state senator, governor or President of the United States. I will miss him greatly, but he will always live within me."

Kirbo, a lawyer, first worked with Carter in 1962 when he argued a vote tampering case that resulted in Carter being elected to the Georgia Senate. He worked behind the scenes during Carter's gubernatorial and presidential campaigns as well as during Carter's terms as governor and president.

Kirbo later helped raise funds for the Carter Presidential Library and was a trustee of the Carter Centre. He declined numerous offers of political appointments including then-Governor Carter's offer to name him to the U.S. Senate seat left vacant by the death of Sen. Richard Russell in 1971.
Kirbo revealed little about his work with Carter, once telling a reporter: "I don't do a lot of damn talking about what I do."
A memorial service was scheduled Thursday afternoon in Atlanta and a graveside service was to take place Friday afternoon in Kirbo's hometown of Bainbridge, Georgia.
